nodes.label: SLOOP firmware
nodes.rationale: Free, open-source (GPL-3.0) firmware for the FM-1, based on Felucca.

nodes.label: Four tracks (3 synth, 1 drum)
nodes.rationale: Three synth tracks share 8 voices; track 4 is the drum machine with its own 6 voices.

nodes.label: Tap and hold (two lives of a button)
nodes.rationale: Tap opens pages; hold opens a layer where keys and knobs do something else. Layer shows after 0.35 s or at once on key/knob use, so a quick tap no longer flashes the layer.

nodes.label: Lock a layer open
nodes.rationale: Hold a layer and tap HOME to keep it open hands-free: one hand on keys, one on knobs.

nodes.label: Recording and overdub
nodes.rationale: Records live and layers every pass on top; notes go to the nearest step as heard, the ~12 ms key-to-sound delay taken back so on-beat lands on-beat.

nodes.label: Free take (loop follows you)
nodes.rationale: On an empty project, play freely with no click or count-in; the loop length and tempo are derived from your playing.

nodes.label: QUANT off (keep your timing)
nodes.rationale: How far off the grid you played becomes the step's nudge, so playback keeps your groove but stays editable step by step.

nodes.label: The step sequencer
nodes.rationale: Each track has up to 64 steps with its own length and division; tracks of different lengths loop independently and stay in phase (polymeters).

nodes.label: Parameter locks
nodes.rationale: Elektron-style: give one sound parameter another value for that step only; 24 locks per track.

nodes.label: Levels (GHOST, SOFT, NORM, HARD)
nodes.rationale: FM-1 keys have no velocity; four levels are chosen with OCT-/OCT+ as you play.

nodes.label: Autosave
nodes.rationale: When stopped and idle for 2.5 s (at most every 20 s), the working project is kept in flash so SLOOP comes back as you left it.

nodes.label: Song mode
nodes.rationale: The FM-1 holds one song: up to 16 steps of 4 sections A-D. For more songs keep one editor backup per song.

nodes.label: Chord mode (one finger, one chord)
nodes.rationale: White keys walk the scale from C4; each chord is built from the scale so it always fits the song.

nodes.label: The sound bank (153 factory sounds)
nodes.rationale: All sounds level-matched (same LEVEL gives same loudness); browsed by kind, then 32 user presets.

nodes.label: Polyphony (voice pool)
nodes.rationale: Three synth tracks share one pool of 8 voices; the drum track has its own 6.

nodes.label: FM6 engine (6-op FM, DX7)
nodes.rationale: msfa, the synthesis core of Dexed; thousands of DX7/Dexed patches play on the FM-1 via SysEx import. The eight EDIT values are macros on top of the patch.

nodes.label: Punch-in effects (27)
nodes.rationale: Run on the whole mix while a key is held and let go cleanly on release; loops/gate locked to tempo. 2.8 adds a settable fade-in/out (0-15).

nodes.label: 2ND CORE (dual-core audio)
nodes.rationale: Sound computed on both FM-1 cores for about twice the CPU headroom; each job checked for corruption and falls back to one core on error instead of crashing.

nodes.label: MIDI clock / SYNC
nodes.rationale: 2.8 reads incoming tempo from the average of the last beats so a steady 140 no longer wavers, while a real tempo change is taken at once.

nodes.label: Bank Select (CC 0)
nodes.rationale: Reaches sounds past the first 128 Program Change range: latched for the next Program Change, bank 0 is the first 128, bank 1 the next, etc.

nodes.label: AUDIO CLK (audio sync click)
nodes.rationale: 2.8.4: a sharp pulse on one audio channel on every clock step to drive Volca / Pocket Operator / Game Boy LSDJ / small modular over a plain 3.5 mm cable; no MIDI-to-sync box. ACLK picks the rate (1PP/2PP/4PP), SIDE the channel (RIGHT for Volca, LEFT for PO). Written at a fixed level after master volume and limiter, so MASTER does not change it.

nodes.label: Scenes (LIVE page)
nodes.rationale: Scenes change how it sounds (knobs), sections change what plays (notes); scenes never change the notes.
